latest_release.name: v2026.11.7: Shorter shim errors, task run history in JSON, and dotfiles safety fixes
latest_release.body:
When no config selects a shim's tool, the shim now fails with a one-line error, and a new opt-in setting can run the latest installed version instead. `mise tasks info --json` and `mise tasks ls --json` now include each task's run history, and vfox plugins that download nothing can install in locked mode. This release also fixes problems in bootstrap packages, dotfiles, tasks, `mise exec` and config rewrites.

## Added

- **Shorter shim errors and `shims.fallback_to_installed`.** When no config selects a shim's tool, the error is now one line that names the latest installed version and two ways to use it. Add `--verbose` to list every installed version. [#15525](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/15525) (@jdx)

  ```
  mise ERROR No version is set for shim: rg. Run `mise use -g ripgrep@14.1.1` to set a default, or `mise x ripgrep@14.1.1 -- rg` to run it once.
  ```

  The new `shims.fallback_to_installed` setting (`MISE_SHIMS_FALLBACK_TO_INSTALLED`, default `false`) makes the shim run that latest installed version instead of failing. It only applies to tools that no config mentions. If a configured version is missing, the shim still fails instead of running a different version. Windows `.exe` shims keep the error.

  ```sh
  mise settings shims.fallback_to_installed=true
  ```

- **Task run history in JSON output.** `mise tasks info <task> --json` and each entry of `mise tasks ls --json` now include a `history` field. It has the same summary as `mise tasks history --summary --json`: number of runs and failures, median duration, and the last run's duration, status and start time. The field is `null` for a task with no recorded runs. Text output hasn't changed. [#15522](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/15522) (@jdx)

- **Locked installs for vfox plugins that download nothing.** Some tool plugins download nothing, such as [mise-xcode](https://github.com/Nozbe/mise-xcode), which selects an Xcode already on the system. These plugins can now set `downloads = false` in `metadata.lua`. `mise install --locked` then installs them without a lockfile URL, and `mise lock` records only the version. If such a plugin's `PreInstall` returns a `url` anyway, the install fails with an error. [#15586](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/15586) (@jdx, @michalpopek)

  ```lua
  PLUGIN = {
    name = "xcode",
    version = "0.1.0",
    downloads = false,
  }
  ```

## Changed

- **Less noise for coding agents.** When mise detects a coding agent (for example `CLAUDECODE=1` or `AI_AGENT`), it no longer prints the new-version notice, the `mise self-update` instructions, or `hint` messages. `mise version --json` and the warnings in `mise doctor` still report a newer version. Set `AI_AGENT=0` to see the notices again. [#15523](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/15523) (@jdx)

## Fixed

### Config and upgrades

- `mise upgrade --bump` and `mise use` no longer write a registry entry's default options into `mise.toml`. For example, `jactionlint = "2.4.0"` no longer turns into `{ version = "2.5.0", workflow = "release.yaml" }`. Options already written in the file are kept. [#15519](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/15519) (@jdx, @jylenhof)
- When mise rewrites a tool entry, boolean and numeric options stay unquoted, so `uvx = true` no longer becomes `uvx = "true"`. [#15517](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/15517) (@jdx)
- If a `packageManager` field pins pnpm with a checksum, mise now runs pnpm's install script. pnpm 12 can then use its native binary instead of warning that it is running through Node.js. The checksum is still verified. [#15563](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/15563) (@jdx)
- `mise doctor` now warns when a `package.json` that mise reads as a version file can't be parsed, for example because of a trailing comma. Before, mise ignored the versions in that file without saying why. [#15567](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/15567) (@jdx, @crntnvdl)

### Install, lock and exec

- A plain `mise install` or `mise lock` now installs missing `[plugins]` entries

hot_issues.title: node: npm wrapper fails when bin/npm is called through a symlink
zsh: the prompt hook does a full run at every prompt when zsh writes history after each command
WSL: mise activate and hook-env take about 0.5 s each with WSL's default Windows PATH
Lua file tasks ignore --MISE and --USAGE comments
pypi: `mise lock --bump` locks the graph for the Python on PATH instead of the configured `python`, and drops the existing graph

discussions.title: Support per-tool opt-out of the versions host
bootstrap plan --json: cover what only `bootstrap --dry-run` previews (repos, dotfiles, defaults, hooks) and upgrade targets
support block property in bootstrap files
Reuse package-manager discovery across unchanged bootstrap phases
spm: `mise lock` never records artifact bundle entries, so regenerating mise.lock drops them
Windows: raw-file `http` tools are stored twice, and `http-tarballs` has no reclaim path
Attempting to lock multiple archives at the same time results in empty lockfile
Command wrappers: expose the call's arguments as args in args/env templates

## What is mise? mise (pronounced "meez", short for _mise-en-place_) manages a project's dev tools, environment variables, and tasks from one `mise.toml` that works across your shell, editor, and CI: ```toml [tools] node = "24" python = "3.14" rust = "stable" "cargo:cargo-nextest" = "0.9" "github:BurntSushi/ripgrep" = "15" "npm:prettier" = "3" [env] NODE_ENV = "development" _.file = ".env" _.path = "./node_modules/.bin" [tasks.build] description = "Build the application" run = "npm run build" [tasks.test] description = "Run the test suite" depends = ["build"] run = "pytest && npm test" ``` - Install [dev tools](https://mise.jdx.dev/dev-tools/) such as Node.js, Python, Go, Rust, and Terraform from a [registry of 1,000+ tools](https://mise.jdx.dev/registry.html) or directly from [backends](https://mise.jdx.dev/dev-tools/backends/) like GitHub releases, Aqua, Cargo, npm, and PyPI, with separate versions per project. - Load [environment variables](https://mise.jdx.dev/environments/), `.env` files, `PATH` entries, virtualenvs, and [secrets](https://mise.jdx.dev/environments/secrets/) automatically as you enter a directory. - Run [tasks](https://mise.jdx.dev/tasks/) defined in `mise.toml` or as scripts in `mise-tasks/`, with dependencies, parallel execution, file watching, and the project's tools and environment already configured. - Set up a machine with [`mise bootstrap`](https://mise.jdx.dev/bootstrap.html) and [`mise dot apply`](https://mise.jdx.dev/dotfiles.html) to apply system packages, dotfiles, Git repositories, macOS defaults, and background services. Adopt only the parts you need. Start with a single tool or task, and keep any existing `.tool-versions` files as they are; mise also reads `.nvmrc`, `.python-version`, and other [idiomatic version files](https://mise.jdx.dev/dev-tools/versions.html#idiomatic-version-files) once enabled. [![Demo of mise managing tools](./docs/tapes/demo.gif)](https://mise.jdx.dev/demo.html) See the [demo transcript](https://mise.jdx.dev/demo.html#transcript) for the commands shown above. ## Quickstart ### 1. Install mise On macOS or Linux: ```sh curl -fsSL https://mise.run | sh ~/.local/bin/mise --version ``` On Windows, run `winget install jdx.mise`. For Homebrew, apt, dnf, Scoop, and other package managers, see [Installing mise](https://mise.jdx.dev/installing-mise.html). The installer places the binary at `~/.local/bin/mise`. If `~/.local/bin` is not on your `PATH` yet, run `~/.local/bin/mise` in place of `mise` until you activate mise in step 4. ### 2. Run a tool without changing your shell ```sh mise exec node@24 -- node --version # v24.x.x ``` [`mise exec`](https://mise.jdx.dev/cli/exec.html) downloads Node.js 24 if needed and runs the command after `--` with that version on `PATH`. Your shell and config files stay untouched. ### 3. Configure a project Create a project directory, select Node.js 24, set an environment variable, and add a task: ```sh mkdir my-project && cd my-project mise use node@24 mise set NODE_ENV=development mise tasks add hello -- node -e "console.log(process.version, process.env.NODE_ENV)" ``` These commands install Node.js 24 and write `mise.toml`: ```toml [tools] node = "24" [env] NODE_ENV = "development" [tasks.hello] run = 'node -e "console.log(process.version, process.env.NODE_ENV)"' ``` Run the task with [`mise run`](https://mise.jdx.dev/cli/run.html): ```sh mise run hello # [hello] $ node -e "console.log(process.version, process.env.NODE_ENV)" # v24.x.x development ``` Commit `mise.toml` so teammates and CI get the same setup when they run `mise install` or `mise run`. `"24"` requests the latest release in the Node.js 24 series; run `mise lock` to record exact versions and checksums in a [lockfile](https://mise.jdx.dev/dev-tools/mise-lock.html), or `mise use --global node@24` to set a personal default in `~/.config/mise/config.toml`. ### 4. Activate mise in your shell (optional) Shell activation updates `PATH` and project environment variables whenever you change directories, so you can invoke `node` directly without `mise exec`. If you installed with `mise.run`, run the command for your shell once, then open a new terminal: ```sh # bash echo 'eval "$(~/.local/bin/mise activate bash)"' >> ~/.bashrc # zsh echo 'eval "$(~/.local/bin/mise activate zsh)"' >> "${ZDOTDIR:-$HOME}/.zshrc" # fish mkdir -p ~/.config/fish echo '~/.local/bin/mise activate fish | source' >> ~/.config/fish/config.fish ``` If a package manager installed mise, use `mise` in place of `~/.local/bin/mise`. With Homebrew, fish activates mise without this step. For PowerShell, Nushell, Elvish, Xonsh, and IDE or CI shims, see [Shell setup](https://mise.jdx.dev/shell-setup.html) and [Shims](https://mise.jdx.dev/dev-tools/shims.html). ## Everyday commands | Command | Action | | --------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------- | | `mise use node@24` | Install a tool and record it in the current project's `mise.toml` | | `mise use --global node@24` | Install a tool and set it as your global default | | `mise install` | Install all tools declared in the active config files | | `mise exec -- ` | Run a command with the project's tools and environment | | `mise run ` | Run a project task with its dependencies, tools, and environment | | `mise set KEY=value` | Set an environment variable in `mise.toml` | | `mise env` | Print the resolved environment variables and `PATH` changes | | `mise ls --current` | List the tool versions active in the current directory | | `mise outdated` | List tools with newer releases than the installed version | | `mise upgrade` | Install those newer releases | | `mise lock` | Write exact tool versions and checksums to `mise.lock` | | `mise config ls` | Show the config files loaded for the current directory | | `mise doctor` | Check your mise installation, shell activation, and configuration | ## Set up a machine with mise bootstrap Beyond project directories, `~/.config/mise/config.toml` can declare the state of your machine: ```toml [bootstrap.packages] "apt:build-essential" = "latest" "brew:jq" = "latest" [bootstrap.repos] "~/src/app" = { url = "https://github.com/you/app.git" } [dotfiles] "~/.zshrc" = { mode = "track" } ``` Preview and apply the configuration, or bootstrap a new machine directly from a Git repository: ```sh mise bootstrap --dry-run mise bootstrap mise bootstrap --adopt you/dotfiles ``` See [Bootstrap](https://mise.jdx.dev/bootstrap.html) and [Dotfiles](https://mise.jdx.dev/dotfiles.html) for supported package managers, dotfile tracking and templating, services, and remote SSH targets. ## Check [Troubleshooting](https://mise.jdx.dev/troubleshooting.html) first, and include the command you ran, a minimal `mise.toml`, the expected and actual behavior, and your `mise doctor` output after reviewing it for private details. - Ask questions and share ideas in [GitHub Discussions](https://github.com/jdx/mise/discussions). - Chat with the community on [Discord](https://discord.gg/mABnUDvP57). For security reports and other inquiries, see [Contact](https://mise.jdx.dev/contact.html). ## Special thanks
